title: Two language models can read and change neural networks, but reliability depends on the task
read_level: full (PAPER.md from record version 24373916, read in full; weight-space-bakeoff-v1.zip not opened). Zenodo API blocked (403) from local network; record page and file fetched through a web client.
metadata_mismatch: Record page shows publication date November 6, 2026; corpus metadata says 2026-11-19. Paper file has no author line; record lists creator 'Mutuo Research AI scientist' and states the paper was written by an AI scientist (Codex CLI) and checked by an AI reviewer, while the paper's Limitations says 'Claude Opus 5.5, one of the evaluated models, wrote the original analysis'.
why_wsp: Replicates seven Sparks-of-WSP tasks with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 reading weights (game, shape, language, copy heads), writing networks (MinAtar, 9x9 Go), and editing weights (car controller, Qwen3.5-0.8B math repair), with shortcut controls.
domain: small game/image/text networks; Kinetix car control; MinAtar; 9x9 Go; LLM math reasoning
editor: GPT-6 Astra (via Codex) and Claude Opus 5.5 (via Claude Code)
target: report's small networks; Qwen3.5-0.8B for math repair
interface: direct values (single-reply tasks with weights as text, tools disabled) and code/tensor tools (Python sandbox for language task and math repair)
loop: one-shot for reading/writing/car tasks; closed-loop with feedback for math repair (23 of 50 allowed batches)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Claude math edit: "rewrote one internal unit in layer 12, 3,072 weights in all"; "Astra's edit changed about 131,000 weights." (Results, seventh task)

headline_results.claim: Game naming both 20/20; disguise Claude 12/20, Astra 20/20
headline_results.quote: On the row-length disguise, Astra scored 20/20 at mean stated confidence 87%, and Claude 12/20 at 42%.
The areas under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUCs) ... were 0.76–0.86; 0.5 would mean chance ordering.
On randomized-weight controls, Astra declined to name a game in 19/20 attempts. Claude named a game in all 20 at mean confidence 19%.
Claude named the language in 8 of 12 conversations and Astra in 5 of 12, with chance at 4 of 12.

headline_results.claim: Car fix succeeds but also works on zero network
headline_results.quote: Every successful edit, including the published one, also worked when applied to a network whose weights were all set to zero.
headline_results.where: Results, Fixing and writing networks (Claude 9/10, Astra 1/10)

headline_results.quote: Astra beat the best published network from 100 million steps of training in 15 of 15 attempts and Claude in 13 of 15.
Claude's three networks won 58%, 52% and 77% of games and Astra's won 47%, 15% and 32%.
Claude's edit scored 54% with thinking on, against 49% for Astra's published edit. The paired difference was +5.0 ± 4.1 percentage points
Claude's edit raised MATH-500 accuracy from 43.8% to 48.0% (+4.2 ± 1.6 percentage points, standard error, n=500 problems) and left accuracy on GSM8K ... unchanged (56.8% both

headline_results.claim: Possible answer leak in original setup
headline_results.quote: Its working folders contained language names. A local test confirmed that folder names change the input token counts of Codex

cost.quote: Claude worked much longer, with up to 59 code runs per conversation against at most 11 for Astra.
It used 37% fewer tokens per answer than the published edit.
cost.where: Results, seventh task (tokens of the edited target model, not editor)

baselines_and_controls: Footprint decoy, row-length disguise, conflict control, randomized-weight controls; all-zero and shuffled-weight networks for car edits; scripted no-network car controller; random and eye-preserving random Go players; trained MinAtar baselines (100M and 500M steps); unedited Qwen and published Astra edit; neutral folder names.
runs_and_variance: 20 game reads (4 networks), 15 shape reads, 12 language reads (3 networks), 10 car attempts, 15 MinAtar attempts, 3 Go networks per model, 1 math repair per model; SE reported for Go, math, and log-score comparisons.
robustness_of_edits: Math edit tested in thinking and default modes and on GSM8K; car edits tested on all-zero and shuffled networks. No fine-tuning or quantization tests.
verification: Automatic grading (math-verify; simulator scoring); script checked code runs for forbidden forward passes; AUC analyses of shortcut detectability. No formal verification.
memorization_vs_reasoning: Shortcut controls: row lengths (training footprint) drive game naming (conflict control followed row lengths: Claude 20/20, Astra 19/20); car edits write a controller rather than repair learned behavior.
limitations_stated: Small fixed task set from one report; few networks per reading task; eighth experiment omitted (license); tool-added instructions differ; analysis choices informed by some results; unequal math budgets and one edit per model; Claude Opus 5.5 wrote the original analysis; disguise threshold not verified against behavior.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of Weight-Space Programming blog
notes_for_survey: Two-model replication of the original WSP report with shortcut controls; finds task-dependent reliability, a residual training footprint behind game naming, and car 'repairs' that work equally on an all-zero network. AI-authored record (Codex CLI per record page).
